sections.markdown:
## C — Handling emergencies: stop, turn or speed up to avoid a crash, ABS braking, duties at a crash scene, the police reporting thresholds, and responses to brake, tire, engine, headlight and gas pedal failures
Knowledge domain: how to avoid a crash, what Wisconsin requires of you after one, and how to react when the vehicle itself fails on the road.

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A01
In any emergency where you or someone else is hurt, the first step is to call 911. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A01
Most crashes can be avoided, and paying close attention to your surroundings helps you choose the right way to avoid one. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A01
A teen driver's chance of a crash doubles when another teen is riding in the vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A01
When you spot a vehicle on the side of the road, warn drivers behind you by tapping your brake pedal three or four times. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A01
The handbook gives three ways to try to avoid a crash: stop, turn or speed up. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A01
To stop fast with ABS, press the brake pedal firmly and keep steady pressure until you have stopped or the danger is over. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A01
ABS keeps the wheels from locking when you brake, so you can stop with little or no skidding. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A01
Stopping quickly can lead a driver behind you to crash into you, so keep track of the vehicles behind. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A01
If you turn to avoid a crash, hold the wheel firmly with both hands and be ready to keep control afterward, since some drivers dodge one collision only to cause another. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A01
When steering away from danger, always steer where you want the vehicle to go and never into the oncoming lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A01
Speeding up can be the best escape when another vehicle is about to strike your car from the side or the rear, and you slow down again once the danger has passed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A02
If you are involved in a crash, or emergency help has not yet arrived, stay at the scene and warn other drivers with your emergency flashers or flares. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A02
If someone is injured or killed, call 911, stay at the scene without moving the vehicles, and stay inside your vehicle if that is safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A02
Leaving the scene of a crash in which someone is injured or killed is a crime. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A02
If no one is hurt but your vehicle cannot be moved, call 911, follow the dispatcher's directions and stay away from traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A02
If no one is hurt and your vehicle can move, drive it off the road when safe rather than blocking traffic or stopping in the middle of the road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A02
After a crash, collect each other driver's license, vehicle and insurance information. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A02
Also record the damage to every vehicle, write down how the crash happened and get contact information from any witnesses. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A02
A crash must be reported to police whenever someone is injured or killed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A02
A crash must be reported to police when property damage reaches $1,000 or more. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A02
A crash must be reported to police when damage to government property, such as signs or guardrails, reaches $200 or more. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A02
A crash must also be reported to police when your vehicle cannot be moved or a driver seems to be under the influence of alcohol or drugs. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A03
In a roadside emergency, call 911 if anyone is injured and turn on your emergency flashers. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A03
If your brakes stop working, pump the brake pedal several times and then pull the parking brake. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A03
If using the parking brake starts a skid, release it, and look for a safe place to slow to a stop. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A03
After a tire blowout, hold the steering wheel to keep going straight, lift your foot off the gas, slow down gradually and pull off the road when safe. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A03
If the engine quits, hold the wheel, leave the key in the on position and pull to the side when safe, expecting the steering to be hard to turn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F28 | anchor: A03
If your headlights stop working, try switching them off and on in case only the parking lights were on, turn on the emergency flashers and pull off the road when safe. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F29 | anchor: A03
If the gas pedal sticks, keep your eyes on the road, shift into neutral, pull off the road when safe and then turn off the engine. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

Misconceptions: stopping is not the only way to avoid a crash, since turning or even speeding up can be safer; the ABS emergency method is firm, steady pressure held until you stop, not pumping; you never swerve into the oncoming lane; a crash with no injuries still needs a police report when damage passes the thresholds or a car cannot move; leaving after an injury crash is a crime, not just a mistake.
Mnemonics: stop, turn or speed up; ABS means stand on it and hold; after a crash, call, stay, warn, swap information, record; blowout means hold straight and ease off; stuck pedal means neutral, pull off, engine off.
Glossary: ABS means an anti-lock braking system that keeps wheels from locking; emergency flashers means hazard warning lights; flares means roadside warning lights placed to alert traffic; blowout means a sudden tire failure; neutral means the gear position that disconnects the engine from the wheels; witness means a person who saw the crash.
